name: Yam Blight (Leaf Blight)
description: A fungal disease causing rapid browning and death of yam leaves and stems. It can spread quickly during warm, wet weather, causing significant defoliation and yield loss.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown rapidly
Rapid browning and necrosis of entire leaves
Blight progressing from lower leaves upward
Stem lesions with white fungal growth near soil
Premature vine death in severe infections
causes: Rhizoctonia solani and Sclerotium rolfsii fungi
Dense foliage with poor air circulation
High soil organic matter with surface debris
treatments: Apply fungicides containing carbendazim or mancozeb
Spray copper oxychloride at first symptoms
prevention: Space yam mounds adequately for air circulation
Provide trellising to keep vines off the ground
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
